title: Les plus secrets mystères des hauts grades de la maçonnerie dévoilés
shelf_note: An 18th-century French exposé of Masonic high-degree rituals; the page is ritual text (Knight of the Sword, Court of Cyrus), as the title says. No collection is given to test it against.
structure_note: There are 205 page records but only 200 distinct page numbers, so 5 records are duplicates. pages_count_field 189 does not match that, and structure pages_translated 0 contradicts pages_translated_field 177, so the counts disagree. The 12 backsteps and 18 repeats are more than misread numerals usually explain. They fit the duplicate records, and perhaps inserted plates or a splice. I cannot confirm which from one page. This page is correctly numbered (printed 117, sig. H iij, matching <page-num>117).

pages.layout: single column of text; running head "DE LA MAÇONNERIE." with page number; quoted speech marked by ,, in the left margin; signature centred at foot

ocr_errors.ocr: ne font plus de la Cour de Cyrus
ocr_errors.image: ne ſont plus de la Cour de Cyrus
ocr_errors.problem: long-s read as f (font for ſont). The translation reads it correctly.

tr_errors.problem: the running head and page number are put into the reading text as a line of body text

other.note: The summary says the candidate is sent "for safe conduct to Jerusalem", and the keywords include "Sixth Degree". The page names neither Jerusalem nor a degree number; both come from outside the page (derived metadata).

missing.english:
I place you in the hands
> ,, of Nabazardin
missing.why: Nabazardin is the biblical Nebuzaradan (Nebuchadnezzar's captain). A general reader will not see that the ritual is acting out the Babylonian exile and the return to rebuild the Temple.

missing.english: knocks seven times in the manner of a Knight of the Sword
missing.why: Knight of the Sword is the name of the Masonic high degree being conferred. Without a note, 'in the manner of' reads as obscure.

book_verdict: The page is a clean, faithful transcription and translation of p. 117. There is one long-s slip that does no harm, and the two glosses are correct. The only flags are book-level: the page counts disagree, and the summary adds details that are not on the page.
